chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah al-Kahili, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about washing the deceased, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Face the undersoles of his feet towards the Qiblah until his face is facing the Qiblah. Then soften his joints, and if it is not possible for you, then leave it. Then begin with his private part with water of lotus and potash, so wash him with three washings, and use plenty of water, and wipe his belly with a gentle wiping.'

Then turn to his head and begin with his right side from his beard and his head. Then do the same with his left side from his head, and his beard, and his face, and wash him with gentleness, and beware of roughness, and wash him with a gentle washing. Then lie him down upon his left side for the right side to be exposed to you. Then wash him from his head to his feet and wipe your hand upon his back and his belly with three washings. Then return him to his right side until the left side is exposed to you, so wash what is between his head and his feet, and wipe your hand upon his back and his belly with three washings.

Then return him to his back and begin with his private part with water of camphor. Do as you did the first time, wash him with three washings with water of camphor and potash, and wipe your hand upon his belly with a gentle wiping. Then turn to his head and do as you did first, with his beard from both its sides, and his head, and his face, with water of camphor with three washings.

Then return him to the left side until the right side is exposed to you, so wash him from his head to his feet with three washings. Then return him to the right side until the left side is exposed to you, so wash him from his head to his feet with three washings. And insert your hand under his shoulders and his forearms, and make the forearm and the palm, along with his side, clean. Every time you wash anything from it, insert your hand under his shoulder and in the inside of his forearms.

Then return him to his back, then wash him with clear water just as you did at first, beginning with the private part. Then turn to the head and the beard and the face until you do just as you did first with clear water.

Then put on a loin cloth on him with a cloth and place the cotton to be under it to pad him with a lot of cotton. Then tighten his thighs upon the cotton with the cloth with an intense tightening until you do not fear that anything might become apparent. And beware of sitting him up or pressing his belly, and beware of placing anything in his ears. So if you were to fear that something might become apparent from his nostrils, so it is not upon you that you stuff it with cotton, and if you do not fear such, so do not make anything to be in it, and do not clean under his nails. Similar to that is the washing of the woman.
ai.seo_question: What is the detailed procedure for washing the deceased according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi provides the definitive Shia methodology for Ghusl al-Mayyit, emphasizing the transition from ritual purity (using lotus and potash) to spiritual fragrance (using camphor) while maintaining the body's dignity through gentle handling. It uniquely prescribes specific orientations and the careful insertion of cotton to prevent leakage, reflecting the Shia emphasis on meticulous adherence to the Imams' instructions for honoring the deceased before burial.
